title: Cumulative proof: from operators back to a boundary problem
promptMarkdown: Let V≥0 be continuous and f continuous on [0,1]. Reconstruct the G^{1/2} argument in the lesson, proving (i) S is compact, self-adjoint and nonnegative; (ii) I+S has an inverse of norm at most one; (iii) the resulting u is C² and satisfies the equation and boundary conditions; (iv) uniqueness. Identify the roles of completeness, Fourier completeness, compactness, and positivity.
hintLadder: Compute the quadratic form of S before discussing its spectrum.
Prove uniform convergence of the G^{1/2} series with Cauchy–Schwarz, then return to the integral formula.
